paper_type_evidence.quote: Using high-resolution ALMA millimeter and JWST infrared data, we analyze the cloud structure and the impact of stellar feedback in the nearest dense cluster-forming region Oph A.

question.value: How do stellar feedback (S1 HII/PDR bubble, protostellar outflows) shape the cloud structure of Oph A, and what faint substellar cores exist, using ALMA 1.3 mm continuum and CO lines plus JWST F470N

evidence.quote: In this paper, through a comparison of ALMA and JWST images of the Oph A region, we aim to uncover the detailed cloud structures of Oph A, with a particular focus on stellar feedback.
in Band 6 during Cycle 2 (PI: F. Nakamura, Project code 2013.1.00839.S)
using the ALMA 12-m Array and the 7-m Array (ACA) in Band 6 during Cycle 2

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Two continuum basebands (2000 MHz each, 128 channels, ~7.4 GHz effective); two line basebands (117.2 MHz, 3840 channels) for 12CO, 13CO, C18O J=2-1

evidence.quote: The remaining two basebands were used for molecular line observations ($^{12}$CO J=2–1, $^{13}$CO J=2–1, C$^{18}$O J=2–1) in dual-polarization mode, with a correlator bandwidth of 117.2 MHz and 3840 channels.

arrays.value: 12-m Array and 7-m Array (ACA), mosaic of 150 and 53 pointings

evidence.quote: We used 150 pointings for the 12 m Array and 53 pointings for the 7 m Array, with spacings of 13.6$''$ and 23.2$''$, respectively.
The uv ranges sampled by the 12-m Array and 7-m Array data were 12.5 – 348 $k \lambda$ and 8.1 – 48 $k \lambda$, respectively.
The final images have a beam size of approximately 1.4$''$$\times$0.9$''$.
The minimum uv distance of the combined data corresponds to a maximum spatial scale of 25$''$.

analysis_steps.goal: Identify faint compact cores in the continuum

method.value: Visual inspection of ALMA continuum and JWST images; criteria peak >8 sigma and more than two closed contours starting at 3 sigma with 1.5 sigma intervals

evidence.quote: (1) The source must exhibit a peak intensity exceeding 8$\sigma$, and (2) It must show more than two closed contours when the dust continuum map is contoured starting at 3$\sigma$ with 1.5$\sigma$ intervals.

validation.value: Cross-check with JWST 4.7 um compact emission to classify protostellar/substellar vs pre-substellar

evidence.quote: cores with 4.7 $\mu$m JWST emission are referred to as protostellar, proto-substellar, or young substellar objects, while those without infrared counterparts are considered prestellar or pre-substellar cores.

method.value: Optically thin dust mass formula with Planck function; Bonnor-Ebert mass ratio alpha_BE = Mc/MBE

evidence.quote: To assess the gravitational boundedness of the four observed cores without associated infrared emission, we calculate the Bonnor-Ebert mass ratio

assumptions.value: Td = 20 K, kappa230GHz = 0.00529 cm2/g (beta=2), gas-to-dust 100, D = 138 pc, tau<1

evidence.quote: $T_d$ is the dust temperature assumed to be 20 K, the opacity $\kappa_{230 \rm GHz} = 0.00529$ cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ with $\beta=2$ (cite: hildebrand83), and the gas-to-dust ratio is set to 100.

validation.value: Temperature sensitivity: 10–30 K changes mass by factor 3.64 to 0.61

evidence.quote: if the temperature varies between 10 K and 30 K, the mass estimate can change by a factor of 3.64 to 0.61.

analysis_steps.goal: Map CO outflows, S1 bubble gas and C18O striations

method.value: 12CO and C18O integrated intensity maps, channel maps, averaged line profiles, position-velocity diagrams; compare with JWST F470N to identify jet driving sources

evidence.quote: In Figure [6](#fig:12COpeak), we show the $^{12}$CO and C$^{18}$O integrated intensity maps.

assumptions.value: Sound speed 0.3–0.5 km/s; B = 0.2 mG lower limit, T = 20 K, n = 1e4 cm-3 for plasma beta

evidence.quote: assuming a magnetic field strength of 0.2 mG (its lower limit), a temperature of 20 K, and a density of $10^4$ cm$^{-3}$

validation.value: Caveat that 12CO is affected by self-absorption and resolved-out emission so peak T is a lower limit

evidence.quote: the observed peak temperature should be considered to be a lower limit of the actual gas kinetic temperature.
CASA pipeline version 4.2.2 and version 4.5.3, for calibration and imaging, respectively

results_numeric.quantity: 1.3 mm flux densities of PSS cores

evidence.quote: The 1.3 mm flux densities of these cores range from 3 mJy to 13 mJy, corresponding to estimated masses of 0.01–0.035 M$_\odot$.
The envelope mass, derived from the 1.3 mm continuum emission, is estimated to be $3.53 \times 10^{-3}$ M$_\odot$.
all four cores without associated infrared emission have Bonnor-Ebert ratios close to unity ($\alpha_{\rm BE} \approx 1$)
\beta \equiv \frac{4\pi c_s^2 \rho}{B^2} \simeq 8.9 \times 10^{-3}
separations of approximately 20–25$''$ , ($\approx 3000-3500$ au

results_numeric.quantity: Mach number of S1 outflowing gas

evidence.quote: the estimated Mach number of the outflow reaches 6–10

findings_qualitative.value: Several new outflows/jets identified from combining 12CO and F470N, including VLA 1623W, [GY92]21, [GY92]23 and a bipolar jet from [GY92]20

evidence.quote: we not only confirmed previously known outflows but also identified new faint outflow candidates and their potential driving sources such as VLA 1623W, \[GY92\]21, and \[GY92\]23.

claims.hypothesis: Faint compact substellar cores exist in Oph A
claims.experiment: Visual identification in 1.3 mm continuum with 8 sigma criterion, JWST cross-match
claims.finding: Four are pre-substellar candidates, three are young substellar objects

evidence.quote: we newly detected 7 substellar cores, three of which show compact near-infrared emission, suggesting they are young substellar objects.

claims.hypothesis: Cores near VLA 1623 may have been ejected
claims.experiment: Morphology of faint CO finger-like structures
claims.result: Weak CO fingers connect cores to VLA 1623

evidence.quote: suggesting they may have been ejected from the close binary VLA1623 Aa+Ab.

claims.hypothesis: S1 bubble shapes Oph A and feeds warm gas toward GSS 30
claims.result: Strong 12CO along eastern ridge edge; northern ridge blown out
claims.finding: Stellar feedback significantly influences cloud structure

evidence.quote: The northern ridge appears “blown out”, with warm gas flowing toward GSS 30, injecting additional turbulent momentum.

claims.experiment: Compare striation orientation with literature B field; PV diagrams
claims.result: Striations align with B; plasma beta ~9e-3; wave-like PV patterns

evidence.quote: position-velocity diagrams show wave-like patterns, possibly reflecting magnetohydrodynamic waves.

why_this_method.value: Visual core identification chosen because spatial filtering biases automated source finders

evidence.quote: can bias automated source-finding algorithms, especially in regions with complex and spatially varying background emission.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Two core formation scenarios considered: turbulent fragmentation vs ejection from VLA 1623

evidence.quote: Two primary formation scenarios are possible for these compact cores: turbulent fragmentation and ejection from a nearby stellar system like VLA 1623A/B.

limitations_admitted.value: Missing flux from interferometric filtering hinders prestellar core detection

evidence.quote: Most prestellar cores have either very weak or undetectable emission, likely due to interferometric spatial filtering.

limitations_admitted.value: Ejected cores may not survive; CO structures affected by missing flux

evidence.quote: The actual structures may be affected by the interferometric missing flux.

referee_caveats_inferred: Core identification is visual and not reproducible by algorithm

Bound-ness from Bonnor-Ebert with assumed T and no kinematics
